title: K1 calibration of N1 inference layer (ollama/gemma)
hypothesis: the N1 LLM layer can recover a known plaintext (K1) from partial cribs + theme
insights: 6 gemma generations; best char-accuracy vs true K1 = 16%, mean 8%. Content words recovered across runs: ['ILLUSION', 'LIGHT', 'NUANCE', 'SHADING', 'SUBTLE'].

CALIBRATION RESULT: N1 reliably recovers the THEME/VOCABULARY of a known plaintext (['ILLUSION', 'LIGHT', 'NUANCE', 'SHADING', 'SUBTLE']) but NOT the exact plaintext (char-accuracy ~8%). N1 is a THEMATIC PRIOR, not a plaintext-recovery tool. This directly explains exp 055: the N1 K4 candidates carry the right themes yet are structurally inadmissible, because exact letter sequence (which KPA needs) is not what N1 produces.
next_steps: if sound: apply the SAME calibration to K2/K3; then trust N1 K4 priors filtered by the exp-055 fanout<=k constraint
if weak: add cross-model N1 (qwen, gemma-31b) and crib-boundary-grammar constraints
